{{about-distinguish|the geometric shape|Bicorne}}

[[Image:Bicone.svg|thumb|100px|right]]

In [[geometry]], a '''bicone''' or '''dicone''' (from {{langx|la|bi-}}, and [[Greek language|Greek]]: ''di-'', both meaning "two") is the three-dimensional [[surface of revolution]] of a [[rhombus]] around one of its [[axes of symmetry]]. Equivalently, a bicone is the surface created by joining two [[Congruence (geometry)|congruent]] [[right circular cone]]s at their bases.
A bicone has [[circular symmetry]] and orthogonal [[bilateral symmetry]].

== Geometry ==
For a bicone with radius <math>r</math> and half-height <math>h</math>, the volume is

:<math>V = \frac{2}{3} \pi r^2 h </math>

and the surface area is

:<math>A =2\pi r \ell\,</math>

where

:<math>\ell = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}</math>

is the [[slant height]].
